title: 5-Year Treasury Note auction — the January block's middle leg, selling on FOMC day one
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 rows. Row reads `5-Year  NOTE / Announcement Thursday, January 21, 2027 / Auction Tuesday, January 26, 2027 / Settlement Monday, February 01, 2027`, with NO trailing `R` against the PDF's own `R --denotes reopening` legend — a new issue, as every monthly 5-Year is. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-21 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because its proposer is the announcement that sizes it. FOMC POSITION, and it is this leg's distinguishing feature: the 2027-01-26/27 FOMC (federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar, fetched direct this session, HTTP 200) makes 2027-01-26 the meeting's FIRST DAY — the 1:00 p.m. ET bidding deadline lands with the committee already in session and the statement still 26 hours away. SIZE EXPECTATION $70B, unchanged at every 5-Year auction since 2024-04-24 (27 auctions, 28 months) on the robust filter, and identical in all six monthly rows sb0590 publishes. DEMAND BASELINE from fiscaldata auctions_query pulled this session (n=134 since 2015): pool bid-to-cover mean 2.425, sd 0.106 — the tightest of the three note legs; the nine that auctioned on an FOMC first day averaged 2.414 (z -0.10), a null. Since 2024-05 the 5-Year has never printed below 2.28. THE DATA TRAP SPECIFIC TO THIS SERIES, found this session and not previously recorded anywhere in this calendar: 5-Year TIPS file as `security_term: 5-Year` under `security_type: Note`, so a naive filter admits 43 TIPS rows and reports the last 5-Year size change as 2026-04-27 (a bogus 26 -> 70 step) instead of the true 2024-04-24; `inflation_index_security: No` is the field that separates them. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
